seen_animation: A black-line doodle of a domed disc (a hat or flying-saucer shape) is turned on its side so the long disc stands nearly vertical at the left and the dome bulges out to the right. Grey scenery is a cloud outline at upper right and a low hill line at lower left. In frames 1-4 the saucer sits in the upper left-center of the frame and edges slightly right. In frames 5-8 it has moved further right and a little lower. In frames 9-12 it drifts back left while staying at about the same lower height. In frames 13-16 it continues left, ending left of where it started, slightly lower than in frame 1. Its lean and shape stay nearly the same throughout; the scenery shifts only by a few pixels.
seen_film: A white entry capsule (wide conical heat shield on the left, small backshell dome on the right) flies tilted against a hazy tan sky with a dark vignette. In frames 1-4 it is in the upper left-center, heat shield angled with its top leaning left. In frames 5-8 it drifts right and slightly down. In frames 9-12 it drifts back left. In frames 13-16 it is further left and lower, and its heat shield edge has turned more upright, showing more of the dome face toward the camera. Frame 14 is slightly blurred. The event is a capsule swaying right then left as it descends, with a gradual change in its tilt.
named_subject: a flying saucer / domed disc standing in for the space entry capsule
evidence: Horizontal position of the saucer tracks the film closely: in frame 1 both objects occupy roughly x 120-205 of the tile; in frames 5-8 both have moved right to roughly x 160-250; in frames 9-12 both return to roughly x 135-245; in frames 13-16 both end at roughly x 80-195, with both drifting slightly lower from frame 9 on. The orientation matches the film: disc edge at left like the heat shield, dome at right like the backshell. Consecutive frames show small, even position changes with no jumps, and the drawing never doubles or is redrawn. The lean of the saucer in frame 16 is about the same as in frame 1, while the film capsule in frames 13-16 is more upright than in frames 1-4.
primary_gap: The saucer keeps one fixed lean for all 16 frames, while the film capsule gradually rotates from a left-leaning tilt in frames 1-4 to a more upright pose facing the camera in frames 13-16.
closes_when: Across frames 9-16 the saucer's long disc axis rotates toward vertical by roughly 10-15 degrees, so that in frames 13-16 the disc edge stands more upright than in frames 1-4, matching the film's change in tilt.
protect: The path (right through frames 5-8, back left through frames 9-16, slight descent) and its timing; the rotated doodle orientation with disc on the left and dome on the right; the doodle's single wobbly outline, the small dot marks on the disc, and the plain dome; the small even per-frame steps with no pops; the quiet grey cloud and hill scenery.
identity_gap: The saucer is clearly the doodle's dome-on-disc drawing with its dot marks, rotated about 70 degrees; the disc is drawn slightly fatter and the dome slightly smaller relative to the disc than in c.png, which is a minor proportion drift rather than a different drawing.
